title: You'll Change
coreMove: Make long commitments with exits that respect the person you may become.
sourcePressure: People underestimate future identity drift and can trap their later selves inside commitments made by an earlier self.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Using change as an excuse to avoid commitment at all.

hook: opening with a generic paycheck scene
opening with a moral lesson about discipline
opening You'll Change with a swapped-in personal finance anecdote
counterintuition: reducing You'll Change to common-sense advice
tryThisNow: write down your values for ninety seconds
asking for a generic money reflection instead of the identity drift move
examples: reusing visible anchors from adjacent chapters instead of identity drift and future self

exampleSpecs.domain: a medical resident choosing a specialty while her interests keep shifting each rotation
exampleSpecs.audience: a trainee avoiding a future-self trap
exampleSpecs.stakes: a prestigious match can lock years around an identity she may outgrow
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes what each rotation made her miss before ranking programs
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a residency rank list beside a stack of rotation badges

exampleSpecs.domain: a couple reviewing mortgage size in a credit union consultation room around possible career changes
exampleSpecs.audience: partners planning for changing priorities without shame
exampleSpecs.stakes: a huge house could trap the later parent, founder, or caregiver they become
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: they test the payment against three future selves before choosing the loan size
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a glass-walled credit union consultation room with two loan estimates on the desk

exampleSpecs.domain: a touring musician signing a five-album contract at age twenty-two
exampleSpecs.audience: an artist thrilled by certainty but blind to identity drift
exampleSpecs.stakes: the contract may make later growth feel like betrayal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he asks for a review clause after reading the album-five delivery date aloud
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a contract page with album-five circled in red ink

exampleSpecs.domain: a city planner choosing modular zoning for a district whose residents are aging
exampleSpecs.audience: a planner leaving room for demographic change
exampleSpecs.stakes: fixed use rules may serve today's voters and fail tomorrow's needs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she walks the board through the same block with twice as many older residents before final zoning
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a foam model of a block with removable use labels

exampleSpecs.domain: a marathon charity founder deciding whether to promise annual races forever
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder respecting future fatigue and organizational change
exampleSpecs.stakes: a permanent promise can turn service into resentment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after the fifth race, she compares volunteer burnout notes with the original founding speech
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a race bib box beside volunteer resignation emails

exampleSpecs.domain: a software engineer negotiating equity with a four-year vesting path during a life transition
exampleSpecs.audience: an employee planning for possible moves, caregiving, and changed ambition
exampleSpecs.stakes: illiquid upside may not match the life she has in year three
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she maps vesting dates against likely relocation and caregiving windows before accepting
exampleSpecs.firstImage: an offer letter open beside a passport renewal form
